correctness.rationale: Correctness PASS on the LCF [12,7,−7]^8 cubic graph, exactly two unordered particles. Independently reconstructed 276/792/558 cubical cells, signed ∂1,∂2, verified ∂1∂2=0 and rank(∂2 mod101)=504. Exhaustively counted 32 seven-cycles, 152 vertex-disjoint unordered pairs, and 32 graph automorphisms. Every product-torus column lies in ker∂2. A 54×54 submatrix has integer determinant +1 and torus rank54, forcing the entire saturated integer kernel, hence H2=Z^54. The seven orbit sizes were regenerated. Exact Smith factors for orbit set {1,3,4} are 51 ones,2,2,4 (index16), whereas {0,1,2,3,5} has 54 units. Exhaustion of all 35 four-orbit unions gives maximal mod2 rank53, and all k=1..4 maxima (31,46,51,53), proving sharp five-orbit threshold rather than simply insufficient examples. Numerical rank modulo101 is a lower bound for Q rank, and kernel dimension upper bound from 54 cycles makes it exact; no incorrect inference from a finite failed search.
residual_risks: No rank/space conclusions for other cages or more than two particles are established.

value.rationale: Scientific value PASS: the McGee graph is the unique cubic girth-seven cage, so its shortest closed paths and automorphism orbits are geometrically canonical. The exact threshold distinguishing rational generation from integer generation is a meaningful new geometric-and-arithmetic invariant: three whole symmetry orbits span rationally while omitting a Z/4 and two Z/2 directions. This is not a routine graph census and provides a concrete sparse nonplanar graph-braid example of integer defects in natural torus generators.
residual_risks: Exact finite-group orbit thresholds for one cage do not prove a general cubic-graph theorem; no such consequence is claimed.

final_claim: For the 24-vertex McGee (3,7)-cage and UConf_2(|G|), the 152 tori from disjoint seven-cycles generate integral H_2≅Z^54. The 32-element symmetry group gives seven torus orbits of sizes (16,32,16,8,32,32,16). No union of at most four orbits generates integrally; orbits (0,1,2,3,5) do. Orbits (1,3,4) span over Q but have quotient (Z/2)^2⊕Z/4.
